subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For source-channel turns that lack a canonical `final_answer` phase, should OpenClaw keep automatic visible replies and trim/suppress interim segments centrally, require explicit message-tool delivery for affected contexts, or add an opt-in final-only delivery mode while preserving current defaults?
rationale: The source bug is real and security-sensitive, but the permanent fix changes the user-visible delivery contract for existing channel deployments and overlaps with the opposite hidden-pre-tool-text problem.

options.title: Central final-only fallback with upgrade guard
options.body: Trim or suppress interim accumulated text at `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` or an equivalent shared boundary, keep explicit finals/message-tool sends visible, and add regression coverage for phase-less transports, cron delivery, and message-tool replies.

options.title: Default to explicit sends for channels
options.body: Move more source-channel contexts to message-tool-only delivery, accepting a stronger safety posture but requiring a migration/documentation plan for deployments that rely on automatic bare text replies.

options.title: Opt-in only for now
options.body: Add a per-channel or per-account final-only option and keep current automatic defaults, reducing compatibility risk but leaving the reported default-path leak open until operators opt in.

recommendation.title: Central final-only fallback with upgrade guard
recommendation.body: Trim or suppress interim accumulated text at `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` or an equivalent shared boundary, keep explicit finals/message-tool sends visible, and add regression coverage for phase-less transports, cron delivery, and message-tool replies.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and PR metadata point to recent ownership of the payload and delivery-mode files that would carry the policy change.
